headline: Citrix confirmed that attackers exploit two NetScaler zero-days for remote code execution, shipped fixes for eight flaws at once, and CISA put both bugs on its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog with a binding federal deadline.

emerging_trends.text: Attackers keep taking the network edge first, and the pattern held this weekend when Citrix confirmed two NetScaler zero-days under exploitation one day after watchTowr warned about them, leaving administrators who pulled appliances off the network vindicated.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Citrix NetScaler Zero-Days Under Active Exploitation

emerging_trends.text: Shared infrastructure carries shared risk: a Cloudflare Containers flaw let one paying customer read residual data left behind by another customer on the same physical host, the kind of tenant-isolation failure that no amount of application hardening inside a container prevents.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Cloudflare Containers Leaked Data Across Tenants

emerging_trends.text: Defenders lose ground quietly, and two findings today measure it: 47 percent of detection rules in the average organization need repair while still showing green on coverage dashboards, and CISA's election security plan names patching friction at state and county election offices as a standing opening for attackers.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Conifers Finds Detection Rules Failing Quietly

topics.title: Citrix NetScaler Zero-Days Under Active Exploitation
topics.latest_developments: Citrix confirmed on September 27, 2026 that attackers exploit CVE-2026-88771, an improper input validation flaw, and CVE-2026-88772, a memory buffer flaw, for remote code execution on NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway, released fixes for those two plus six more vulnerabilities running through CVE-2026-88778, and CISA added both exploited bugs to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog; one of the two reaches every deployment on an affected version, including appliances in the default configuration.
topics.summary: NetScaler ADC and Gateway terminate remote access and load-balance applications for enterprises worldwide, and remote code execution on one hands an attacker the network edge. Install the Citrix updates now and hunt for signs of compromise on any appliance that sat exposed before the patch.

sources.title: Warning: Two Unpatched Citrix NetScaler RCE Zero-Days Under Active Exploitation
Citrix confirms two NetScaler RCE zero-days exploited in attacks
Critical Zero-Day Vulnerabilities Exploited in Citrix NetScaler ADC, Gateway
CISA Adds Two Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog

topics.title: SharePoint Exploitation Puts Agencies on a Monday Deadline
topics.latest_developments: SecurityWeek reported on September 27, 2026 that attackers now exploit CVE-2026-65660 in the wild, and the CISA patching deadline for federal agencies falls Monday, September 28, 2026.
topics.summary: CVE-2026-65660, rated 8.8, is a code injection flaw in Microsoft Office SharePoint Server that gives an authenticated user remote code execution; CISA listed it alongside CVE-2026-67279 in MikroTik RouterOS. Patch both, and treat any internet-facing SharePoint server as a priority.

sources.title: Microsoft SharePoint Flaw CVE-2026-65660 Now Exploited in Attacks
SharePoint RCE and MikroTik RouterOS Flaws Actively Exploited in the Wild

topics.title: Scareware Ads and the Macfinger ClickFix Campaign
topics.latest_developments: Ars Technica reported on September 25, 2026 that Google ad placements across the internet deliver scareware that freezes a Mac and tells its owner the machine carries an infection, and the SANS Internet Storm Center published a breakdown of the malware behind the Macfinger ClickFix campaign the same day.
topics.summary: Both routes convince the person at the keyboard to act: the ad fakes an infection warning, and ClickFix lures hand the victim a command to paste. Train staff to treat any browser page claiming an infection as hostile, and block the paste-and-run pattern at the endpoint.

sources.title: Your uncle's frozen Mac says it's infected after viewing a Google ad. Now what?
A Closer Look at Malware From the Macfinger ClickFix Campaign, (Fri, Sep 25th)

topics.title: Wireshark Patches 19 Flaws as an Office Update Deactivates Licenses
topics.latest_developments: The Wireshark project shipped release 4.6.9 on September 27, 2026, closing 19 vulnerabilities and 16 bugs in the packet analyzer that sits on nearly every incident responder's laptop, and Microsoft halted the rollout of the KB5002907 Microsoft 365 update after it deactivated and in some cases removed perpetual Office 2016 and Office 2019 installations.
topics.summary: Wireshark parses untrusted capture files, so a malformed packet trace turns its dissectors into an attack surface against the analyst; update to 4.6.9. Organizations running perpetual Office licenses alongside Microsoft 365 should hold KB5002907 until Microsoft resumes the rollout.

sources.title: Wireshark 4.6.9 Released, (Sun, Sep 27th)
Microsoft pauses KB5002907 update after Office license deactivations

topics.title: Cloudflare Containers Leaked Data Across Tenants
topics.latest_developments: Cloudflare fixed a vulnerability in its Containers and Sandboxes products, BleepingComputer reported on September 27, 2026, that let any customer holding a Workers Paid account recover residual data from other customers' containers sharing the same physical host.
topics.summary: Containers and Sandboxes run customer workloads on Cloudflare's shared fleet, and the flaw broke the isolation boundary that separates one tenant's leftover data from the next tenant on the machine. Cloudflare deployed the fix on its own platform, so customers take no action, though anyone who ran sensitive workloads on the service should weigh what data the containers held.

sources.title: Cloudflare fixes Containers cross-tenant flaw exposing customer data

topics.title: A Cyberattack Disrupts Dyfed-Powys Police
topics.latest_developments: Dyfed-Powys Police, the force covering southwest and mid Wales, said on September 25, 2026 that a cyberattack knocked out some of its non-emergency systems and may have exposed staff information.
topics.summary: The force kept emergency response running while it worked through the outage and assessed what attackers reached. Police staff records carry home addresses and personal details that make officers targets, so the exposure question matters more than the downtime.

sources.title: Cyberattack hits Welsh police force, may have affected staff data

topics.title: CISA Delivers an Election Security Plan
topics.latest_developments: CISA published the election security plan that Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin ordered in July 2026, and it flags attacks on voter registration databases and the barriers that keep election offices from patching their systems.
topics.summary: State and county election offices run the machinery of American voting on small budgets and thin staff, which leaves known vulnerabilities open for months. The plan sets out what the agency will do about both problems ahead of the next federal election cycle.

sources.title: CISA Election Security Plan Flags Patching Barriers, Voter Database Attacks

topics.title: Conifers Finds Detection Rules Failing Quietly
topics.latest_developments: Conifers assessed 14,652 detection rules across its customer base and found that 47 percent of the detections in the average organization need attention, with failures falling into five groups that start with logic bugs.
topics.summary: The study covered rules customers wrote themselves and rules vendors manage inside SIEM, endpoint, cloud, identity, email, and network tools. A rule can show as deployed on a coverage dashboard and still never fire when an attacker uses the technique it targets, so test detections against real technique execution instead of trusting the dashboard.

sources.title: Threat detection dashboards are masking security coverage gaps

business_politics.title: Iran Pressed to Trade Nuclear Concessions for Talks
business_politics.latest_developments: Mediators are pressing Tehran to offer nuclear concessions to restart negotiations with Washington, the Wall Street Journal reported Sunday, September 27, a bid the mediators themselves call a long shot after President Trump rejected Iran's seven-day truce proposal.
business_politics.summary: The seven-month war has closed the Strait of Hormuz, and Trump told the Wall Street Journal he expects American bombing to resume after the November 3 midterm elections. The concession track is the only thing standing between the current fighting and all-out war across the Gulf, and the oil, tanker, and gas markets price every turn of it.

sources.title: Iran Pressed to Make Nuclear Concessions to Revive Peace Talks With U.S.

business_politics.title: Explosives Arrests at the British Base Flying Iran Strikes
business_politics.latest_developments: British police arrested five men near RAF Fairford on Sunday, September 27, on suspicion of preparing a terrorist act, counter-terrorism officers took over the case, and President Trump suggested American agencies worked with the United Kingdom to stop an attack; investigators are examining whether the suspects have ties to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.
business_politics.summary: RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire hosts the American long-range bombers running missions in the war with Iran, and police declared a major incident, sent bomb disposal teams to the scene, and evacuated homes near the perimeter. Iran has warned Britain of consequences for hosting the flights, which carries the war onto British soil.

sources.title: Explosives arrests made in ‘major incident’ near RAF Fairford
U.K. Arrests Five in Suspected Terrorist Plot Near Air Base Used by U.S.

business_politics.title: Swiss Voters Rule on Neutrality
business_politics.latest_developments: Swiss voters rejected the neutrality measure Sunday, September 27, with 68.4% opposed, leaving Bern free to keep cooperating with military alliances.
business_politics.summary: The referendum would have barred Switzerland from working with any military alliance unless an enemy attacked it first, writing centuries of practice into a hard constitutional rule. Defeat preserves the quiet defense cooperation Bern has built with European partners since Russia invaded Ukraine, including joint procurement and air-defense coordination.

sources.title: Swiss voters to decide fate of centuries-old neutrality policy

business_politics.title: Europe and Asia Head Into an LNG Bidding War
business_politics.latest_developments: The Financial Times reported Sunday, September 27, that European Union gas storage sits at record lows heading into winter, setting up intensifying competition with Asian buyers for liquefied natural gas cargoes over the coming months.
business_politics.summary: The war with Iran and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz have thinned the pool of seaborne cargoes just as Europe enters the heating season with its tanks emptier than at any point on record. Every cargo Asia outbids Europe for pushes European gas and power prices higher and squeezes energy-intensive industry, which has already idled plants in Britain.

sources.title: Europe braces for LNG tug of war with Asia

business_politics.title: Private Credit Redemptions Slow
business_politics.latest_developments: Redemption requests from retail investors in private credit funds fell, the Financial Times reported Sunday, September 27, easing the withdrawal pressure that had built through the summer, though fund managers told the paper it remains too early to call the bottom.
business_politics.summary: Retail money in semi-liquid private credit vehicles had been heading for the exits, forcing managers to meet redemptions out of a portfolio of loans that trade rarely. A slower pace of withdrawals relieves the funding mismatch that banks lending into the sector watch most closely.

sources.title: Private credit turmoil eases as investor withdrawals slow

business.title: Brickworks Breaks Ground in the Strip District
business.latest_developments: Developers held the groundbreaking Sunday, September 27, for Brickworks, a luxury housing project in the heart of Pittsburgh's Strip District, WPXI reported.
business.summary: The Strip District has absorbed a decade of warehouse conversions, robotics tenants, and new apartments along Smallman and Railroad streets. Brickworks adds market-rate units to a neighborhood whose residential pipeline now competes with the downtown office conversions taking shape a mile west.

sources.title: Groundbreaking held for ‘Brickworks’ luxury development in Pittsburgh’s Strip District

business.title: CCAC Faculty Rally Over Their Contract
business.latest_developments: Community College of Allegheny County faculty members rallied Saturday, September 26, at the college's North Side campus as contract negotiations with the administration continue.
business.summary: CCAC runs four campuses across Allegheny County and enrolls the region's largest body of two-year students. The faculty took their bargaining fight outdoors on the North Side the same weekend the college marked its 60th year.

sources.title: CCAC faculty rally at North Side campus amid contract negotiations

business.title: Washington County Opens a Flood Recovery Center
business.latest_developments: Washington County will host a Multi-Agency Response Center to help residents and business owners recover from the storm damage and flooding of the past two weekends, WPXI reported Sunday, September 27.
business.summary: Two straight weekends of heavy rain pushed Chartiers Creek and other streams over their banks, swamping buildings along Jefferson Avenue in Canton Township and prompting the township to declare a state of emergency on September 20. The response center gathers aid agencies in one place so flooded households and businesses can file damage claims and reach recovery programs without chasing them separately.

sources.title: Washington County floods: Response center to aid residents, businesses recovering from storm damage

around_town.title: Fetterman Sees a Democratic Senate and Keeps His Own Plans Open
around_town.latest_developments: U.S. Senator John Fetterman told KDKA on Sunday, September 27, that it is "entirely possible" Democrats win control of the Senate in the November 3 midterms, and he answered questions about his own future by saying, "let's revisit after the midterm."
around_town.summary: Fetterman, the Pennsylvania Democrat who has spent the term feuding with his party's left flank, faces a likely primary challenge in 2028 without a settled political base. His refusal to commit keeps open the question of whether he seeks reelection, switches parties, or leaves the seat.

sources.title: Sen. John Fetterman says it's "entirely possible" Democrats take back Senate, says "let's revisit after the midterm" on his plans

around_town.title: A Bill to Keep AI Out of the Teacher's Chair
around_town.latest_developments: Duquesne University education dean Gretchen Givens Generett wrote in TribLive on Sunday, September 27, that state Senator Lindsey Williams will introduce the Human Students Need Human Educators bill, which would bar artificial intelligence from serving as the teacher of record.
around_town.summary: The measure would cover Pennsylvania public and charter schools from kindergarten through 12th grade, the State System of Higher Education, the state-related universities, and community colleges. Generett argues artificial intelligence belongs in classrooms as a tool and never at the front of the room, and the bill lands as faculty unions in Pittsburgh write similar protections into contract talks.

sources.title: Gretchen Givens Generett: AI belongs in education, but not at the front of the classroom

around_town.title: The Cathedral of Learning Turns 100
around_town.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette published two pieces Sunday, September 27, marking the centennial of the University of Pittsburgh's Cathedral of Learning, one tracing how the tower became a Pittsburgh landmark and one collecting readers' memories of the building they call Cathy.
around_town.summary: The Gothic skyscraper anchors Pitt's Oakland campus, holds the Nationality Rooms, and serves as classroom space and civic symbol at once. The anniversary lands as Pitt runs the $3 billion "Proving Possible" fundraising campaign it opened September 25.

sources.title: How Pitt's Cathedral of Learning has remained a beacon in Pittsburgh as it hits 100

around_town.title: The Races That Decide Harrisburg
around_town.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette laid out Sunday, September 27, the specific 2026 legislative contests that will determine which party controls the Pennsylvania House and Senate, with the election five weeks off on November 3.
around_town.summary: Democrats hold the Pennsylvania House by a single seat and Republicans hold the Senate, so a handful of suburban and Western Pennsylvania districts decide whether Governor Josh Shapiro governs with a split legislature or a friendlier one. Allegheny County mailed roughly 120,000 ballots to voters starting last weekend.

sources.title: The 2026 races that could decide control of the Pennsylvania House and Senate

around_town.title: The Nor'easter Sends Clouds and Little Else
around_town.latest_developments: The nor'easter held its rain east of Western Pennsylvania through Sunday, September 27, and WPXI's evening update calls for spotty showers mainly east of Pittsburgh, overnight temperatures in the 50s, and clouds to open the workweek.
around_town.summary: The storm flooded the Atlantic coast for a second day and knocked out power to more than 130,000 customers in the Northeast while leaving Pittsburgh dry and breezy. The Laurel Highlands ridges carried the region's best shower chance, and the 1 p.m. kickoff at Acrisure Stadium stayed inside the dry stretch.

sources.title: Clouds increase as nor’easter moves inland; little rain expected in Pittsburgh region
Few spotty showers possible this evening, clouds kick off the workweek
Western PA: Cloudy and breezy with few light showers
Seasonable temperatures remain in Pittsburgh on Sunday with some light rain possible

around_teams.title: The Offense Wakes Up Against Cincinnati
around_teams.latest_developments: The Steelers' offense came alive against the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday, September 27, at Acrisure Stadium, with running back Jaylen Warren carrying the load, and Post-Gazette columnist Noah Hiles called the game a Mike McCarthy masterpiece.
around_teams.summary: Pittsburgh entered AFC North play with the NFL's worst offense, running back Rico Dowdle hurt and rookie lineman Gennings Dunker on injured reserve, and Aaron Rodgers matched Joe Burrow throw for throw while defensive lineman Derrick Harmon made plays on the other side. McCarthy, Rodgers, and Harmon took questions afterward, Cam Heyward and his co-host streamed a postgame show on Not Just Football, and the Post-Gazette report card handed Warren its top marks; the Steelers play at Cleveland on Thursday night.

sources.title: Noah Hiles: Steelers’ victory against the Bengals was a Mike McCarthy masterpiece
The Steelers’ offense finally comes alive in a wild home victory against the Bengals
Steelers report card: Running back Jaylen Warren comes up big against the Bengals

sources.source: Not Just Football with Cam Heyward

Coach Mike McCarthy Postgame Press Conference (Week 3 vs Bengals) | Pittsburgh Steelers

around_teams.title: Porter Sits Out a Third Straight Game
around_teams.latest_developments: The Steelers listed cornerback Joey Porter Jr. among their inactives again Sunday, September 27, against the Cincinnati Bengals, the Post-Gazette reported.
around_teams.summary: Porter has stayed out of uniform through a contract standoff with general manager Omar Khan, and Asante Samuel Jr. has taken his place in the secondary and played well. Rod Woodson and Darren Perry fought the Steelers over contracts in the 1990s and finished their Pittsburgh careers anyway, the precedent the Post-Gazette raised last week as Porter's absence stretched on.

sources.title: Steelers CB Joey Porter Jr. is inactive again for Sunday’s game against the Bengals

around_teams.title: The Pirates Finish Above .500
around_teams.latest_developments: The Pirates closed their season at Comerica Park in Detroit on Sunday, September 27, with a winning record, their first since 2018, the Post-Gazette reported, with rookie Konnor Griffin and right-hander Jared Jones figuring in the finale.
around_teams.summary: Pittsburgh improved by 11 wins over 2025 and still missed the playoffs. General manager Ben Cherington told the Post-Gazette on Saturday that he expects to return for 2027 and backed manager Don Kelly to keep the job, and ace Paul Skenes finished a season he traced to his workload at the World Baseball Classic.

sources.title: The Pirates beat the Tigers in their season finale to finish 2026 with a winning record
Pirates general manager Ben Cherington says he expects to be back in 2027

team_usa.title: Eleven Debuts in a 4-1 Win Over Peru
team_usa.latest_developments: ESPN reported Sunday, September 27, that Mauricio Pochettino handed out 11 debuts in the United States' 4-1 win over Peru in Orlando, Florida, eight of them to teenagers, and that the coach called himself "so proud" and said the play gave him goosebumps.
team_usa.summary: The friendly Saturday, September 26, was the American men's first match since the 2026 World Cup and the opening of the cycle toward 2030. Sebastian Berhalter drew a 10 and Justin Ellis a 9 in ESPN's player ratings, and 16-year-old Cavan Sullivan started, the youngest American to do so since Freddy Adu in 2006.

sources.title: Poch 'so proud' as 8 teens debut in USMNT rout
USMNT player ratings: Ellis gets 9, Berhalter 10 in Peru rout
There's a palpable sense of excitement surrounding the USMNT's young guns
